718: Available money. It can go negative (overdraft), but you pay very high interest.
720: Valuation: annual EBITDA × multiple + cash + bonds + inventory − debt. It sets your rank.
723: Economic activity index (1.00 = normal). Affects demand according to each product's income elasticity.

738: Your company is worth %s. You did it in %d minutes of play (%s years in game).
739: Game over. Want more titles? Try investor mode.
740: You reached the top. You can keep playing as long as you like.
743: You'll choose a slot for the new game. The current one is saved now in its slot.
748: Read the odds: expected value and risk don't always go together (see Concepts).
750: Money available to invest and pay costs.
754: Price × units sold so far this month.
757: What's left after ALL costs, interest, depreciation and taxes.
759: How much an investor would pay for your company. The multiple rises in a boom and falls in a recession.
764: Revenue and EBITDA per day (7-day average)
767: All good. Look for the next investment with the best return.

793: Contribution = revenue − goods − salaries − branch rent (last closed month). Annual ROI = contribution × 12 ÷ total investment in the branch.
796: Stars: %s of 5 (with 5 it sells 15%% more than with 3; they rise by serving everyone, with good reputation, quality and a fair price). Total investment: %s. Book value: %s. Productivity: %s %s per employee per day.
797: Fire: you pay %d days of salary as severance.
799: Expand to %s for %s: more traffic and room for more employees.

812: How much demand rises or falls with the economy.
816: Part of the inventory lost each day.
820: Licenses, recipes and development. Recorded as an intangible asset and amortized over 5 years.

823: Demand drops when you raise the price (elasticity). The best price isn't the highest or the lowest: it's the one that maximizes sales × margin.

828: What the competition charges for this quality. Rises with inflation.
